course: Small Machines & Pharmaceuticals: The Complete Import Business
module_title: Sourcing Pharmaceuticals (Veterinary) from India and China

lessons.title: The Veterinary Medicine Market in Africa
lessons.body: Africa's livestock population is huge: over 400 million cattle, 500 million goats, and 1 billion poultry. Yet veterinary drug supply is fragmented. Most countries import 80-90% of their veterinary pharmaceuticals. The market is growing at 8-10% per year due to rising meat demand and disease outbreaks like African Swine Fever and Newcastle disease. Key products include antibiotics (oxytetracycline, penicillin), antiparasitics (ivermectin, albendazole), vaccines (Newcastle, Gumboro), and vitamins. Small-scale importers can start with a 20-foot container of mixed products worth $15,000-$30,000. But you must know your local demand. In Kenya, for example, the top-selling vet drugs are dewormers and antibiotics for dairy cattle. In Nigeria, poultry vaccines dominate. Start by visiting local agrovet shops and veterinary clinics to see what they stock and what runs out. Also check government tenders: many ministries of agriculture buy vet drugs in bulk. A single tender can be worth $50,000. But you need to be registered. The market is price-sensitive: farmers will pay for quality but compare prices. Chinese and Indian generics are 30-50% cheaper than European brands. Your competitive edge is reliable supply and credit terms. Many local vets will buy from you if you offer 30-day payment. So you need working capital. A good starting point is to focus on one species (e.g., poultry) and one product category (e.g., vaccines). Build relationships with 10-20 regular customers. Then expand. Remember: veterinary drugs are regulated. You cannot just import any product. You need permits. But the demand is there. In 2022, Africa imported over $1.2 billion in veterinary pharmaceuticals. The top suppliers were India, China, and South Africa. Your opportunity is to tap into that supply chain at a small scale.

lessons.title: Indian Veterinary Pharmaceutical Suppliers
lessons.body: India is the world's largest supplier of generic veterinary drugs. Companies like Cipla, Sun Pharmaceutical, Zydus, and Intas have veterinary divisions. But for small importers, you want mid-sized manufacturers in Gujarat, Hyderabad, and Mumbai. Key hubs: Ahmedabad (Gujarat) for antibiotics, Hyderabad for APIs and formulations, and Pune for vaccines. How to find suppliers? Use IndiaMART and TradeIndia. Search for 'veterinary oxytetracycline manufacturer' or 'ivermectin injection supplier'. You'll get hundreds of results. Filter by 'verified' and 'GST registered'. Then request quotes. A 20-foot container of oxytetracycline 20% injection (100ml bottles) might cost $8,000-$12,000 FOB. Always ask for a proforma invoice with HS code, packing list, and lead time. Payment terms: typically 30% advance, 70% against BL copy. For first orders, use LC or escrow. Indian suppliers often require minimum order quantity (MOQ) of 1,000-5,000 bottles per product. But some will do mixed containers. You must verify the supplier's drug license and GMP certificate. Ask for a copy of their WHO-GMP or state FDA license. Also check if they have export experience to Africa. Many Indian suppliers are familiar with Nigerian NAFDAC and Kenyan PPB requirements. They can provide dossiers for registration. A good supplier will also help with artwork for your own brand. Expect to pay $200-$500 for registration support. Shipping from Nhava Sheva or Mundra to Mombasa or Lagos takes 20-35 days. Air freight is faster but expensive ($5-$8 per kg). For small starts, air freight for 100kg is possible. But sea is cheaper for volume. Build relationships: visit India if you can. Attend Vet Expo India or IPHEX. Otherwise, video calls and WhatsApp are fine. Always start with a small trial order to test quality and shipping.

lessons.title: Chinese Veterinary Drug Manufacturers
lessons.body: China is the second-largest supplier of veterinary drugs to Africa, after India. Chinese manufacturers are strong in antibiotics, antiparasitics, and feed additives. Key hubs: Hebei, Shandong, and Zhejiang provinces. Companies like Hebei Yuanzheng, Shandong Lvdu, and Zhejiang Hisun are major players. But for small importers, you'll find many trading companies on Alibaba and Made-in-China. Search for 'veterinary ivermectin injection' or 'oxytetracycline powder'. Prices are often 10-20% lower than India, but quality can vary. Always ask for a GMP certificate. Chinese GMP (or cGMP) is acceptable in many African countries, but some require WHO-GMP. You must check with your local veterinary authority. A typical order: 1,000 kg of oxytetracycline HCl powder for $20-$30 per kg FOB. That's $20,000-$30,000. For finished products, a 20-foot container of 100ml injections might cost $7,000-$10,000. Payment: 30% T/T advance, 70% against B/L copy. Chinese suppliers often accept smaller MOQs than Indian ones. Some will do as low as 500 bottles per SKU. But shipping from Shanghai or Qingdao to Africa takes 25-40 days. Air freight is available from Guangzhou. Quality control is critical: request a pre-shipment sample. Test it locally or send to a lab. In Africa, labs like SGS or Bureau Veritas can test for potency and sterility. Cost: $200-$500 per sample. Always inspect the factory via video call. Ask for their export license and business license. Many Chinese suppliers are trading companies, not manufacturers. That's okay, but you pay a markup. To get better prices, ask for the manufacturer's contact directly. But be careful: some Chinese suppliers sell counterfeit or substandard drugs. Always use a reputable inspection company like AsiaInspection or QIMA. For a $30,000 order, inspection costs $300-$500. Worth it. Build long-term relationships: visit Canton Fair or attend VIV Asia. Otherwise, use Alibaba Trade Assurance for first orders.

lessons.title: GMP Certification for Veterinary Products
lessons.body: GMP stands for Good Manufacturing Practice. It's a set of rules that ensures drugs are made consistently and safely. For veterinary products, GMP covers premises, equipment, personnel, hygiene, and documentation. When importing from India or China, you must verify that the manufacturer has a valid GMP certificate. There are different types: WHO-GMP, EU-GMP, and national GMP (like Indian state FDA or Chinese cGMP). WHO-GMP is the most widely accepted in Africa. Many African countries require WHO-GMP for registration. For example, Nigeria's NAFDAC and Kenya's PPB insist on WHO-GMP for veterinary drugs. How to check? Ask the supplier for a copy of the certificate. Then verify with the issuing authority. For WHO-GMP, check the WHO website or the national drug authority. For Indian suppliers, check the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) website. For Chinese, check the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Don't just accept a PDF: call or email the authority. Also, check the certificate's scope: does it cover the specific product you're buying? A GMP certificate for tablets doesn't cover injections. You need GMP for each dosage form. If a supplier cannot provide GMP, walk away. Counterfeit or substandard vet drugs can kill animals and harm your reputation. In Africa, many countries also require a Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (CPP) from the exporting country's drug authority. This is a document that confirms the product is approved for use in the exporting country. For India, CPP is issued by CDSCO. For China, by NMPA. Getting a CPP can take 4-8 weeks. Your supplier should handle it. But you must request it. Some suppliers charge $100-$300 for CPP. Also, GMP certificates expire. Check the expiry date. Renewal is typically every 2-3 years. Always keep copies for your records. When you register your product in Africa, you'll need to submit these documents. So start collecting them early.

lessons.title: Import Permits and Veterinary Authority Approval
lessons.body: You cannot import veterinary drugs without a permit. Every African country has a veterinary authority that regulates imports. Examples: Nigeria's NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control), Kenya's PPB (Pharmacy and Poisons Board), South Africa's DAFF (Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries), and Ghana's FDA. The process is similar: you need to register the product, get an import permit, and clear customs. First, register your company with the relevant authority. You'll need a business license, tax ID, and a physical address. Then, for each product, submit a dossier. The dossier includes: GMP certificate, CPP, product specification, method of analysis, stability data, labeling, and samples. Registration fees vary: $500-$2,000 per product. It can take 3-12 months. Once registered, you apply for an import permit for each shipment. The permit specifies quantity, batch number, and expiry date. You must also have a warehouse that meets storage requirements. The authority may inspect it. For vaccines, you need cold chain storage. For antibiotics, you need dry, cool storage. After the permit is issued, you can place your order. When goods arrive, customs will ask for the permit, invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin. You also need to pay import duty and VAT. In many countries, veterinary drugs are exempt from duty but not VAT. Check your local tariff. For example, in Kenya, vet drugs are zero-rated for VAT. In Nigeria, they are exempt from import duty but 7.5% VAT applies. Clearance can take 1-2 weeks if documents are correct. Use a customs agent who knows veterinary imports. Expect to pay $200-$500 for clearance. Always keep copies of all permits and certificates. Renewals are annual. If you import without a permit, your goods will be seized and you may be fined or banned. So follow the rules. Start with one product and one country. Learn the process. Then expand.

lessons.title: Cold Chain and Storage Requirements
lessons.body: Many veterinary pharmaceuticals require specific storage conditions. Vaccines are the most sensitive: they must be kept at 2-8Â°C from factory to farm. Antibiotics and antiparasitics are usually stable at room temperature (15-25Â°C) but must be protected from light and moisture. If you import vaccines, you need a cold chain. This means refrigerated containers, cold rooms, and refrigerated vehicles. A 20-foot refrigerated container costs $3,000-$5,000 to ship from India to Africa, plus $100-$200 per day for power. You also need a cold room at your warehouse: a 10mÂ³ cold room costs $5,000-$10,000. For small-scale importers, it's often better to start with non-cold-chain products like dewormers and antibiotics. Then, once you have volume, invest in cold chain. For storage, you need a dry, well-ventilated warehouse. Temperature should not exceed 25Â°C. Humidity should be below 60%. Use pallets to keep boxes off the floor. Stack boxes at least 30cm from walls. Keep records of temperature and humidity. Use a data logger ($50-$100) to monitor. For vaccines, you need a backup generator in case of power cuts. In many African cities, power is unreliable. A small generator costs $300-$500. Also, train your staff on handling. They must know not to leave vaccines in the sun. Use cool boxes with ice packs for delivery. For last-mile delivery to farms, a vaccine carrier costs $20-$50. Always check expiry dates. Use FIFO (First In, First Out). If a product expires, you must dispose of it properly. In Kenya, for example, you must return expired drugs to the PPB for destruction. Never sell expired drugs. It's illegal and dangerous. For antibiotics, store in a cool, dry place. Keep away from direct sunlight. Some liquids need protection from freezing. Read the label. When shipping, insist on temperature-controlled containers for vaccines. For other products, a standard container is fine. But always ask the supplier for storage instructions. Include them in your warehouse SOP.

quiz.q: What percentage of veterinary pharmaceuticals does Africa import?
quiz.explanation: Most African countries import 80-90% of their veterinary drugs due to limited local manufacturing.

quiz.q: Which product category dominates the veterinary market in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria has a large poultry industry, so poultry vaccines are in high demand.

quiz.q: What is a common payment term for first orders from Indian suppliers?
quiz.explanation: Indian suppliers typically require 30% advance and the balance against bill of lading copy for first orders.

quiz.q: Which Indian city is a hub for veterinary vaccine manufacturing?
quiz.explanation: Pune is known for vaccine production, while Ahmedabad and Hyderabad are hubs for antibiotics and APIs.

quiz.q: What document confirms that a product is approved for use in the exporting country?
quiz.explanation: The CPP is issued by the exporting country's drug authority and confirms the product's approval there.

quiz.q: Which Chinese province is a major hub for veterinary drug manufacturing?
quiz.explanation: Hebei province, along with Shandong and Zhejiang, is a key hub for veterinary drug production in China.

quiz.q: What is the typical MOQ for Indian veterinary drug suppliers?
quiz.explanation: Indian suppliers often require a minimum order quantity of 1,000-5,000 bottles per product.

quiz.q: Which organization issues WHO-GMP certificates?
quiz.explanation: WHO-GMP is issued by national drug authorities that follow WHO guidelines, not by WHO directly.

quiz.q: What is the cost of a pre-shipment inspection for a $30,000 order from China?
quiz.explanation: Inspection companies like AsiaInspection or QIMA charge $300-$500 for a typical pre-shipment inspection.

quiz.q: Which African country's veterinary authority is called NAFDAC?
quiz.explanation: NAFDAC is the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control in Nigeria.

quiz.q: What is the typical registration fee per product for veterinary drugs in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Registration fees vary but typically range from $500 to $2,000 per product.

quiz.q: Which storage condition is required for veterinary vaccines?
quiz.explanation: Vaccines must be kept at 2-8Â°C to maintain potency.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a Certificate of Origin?
options: B) To confirm the country of manufacture
quiz.explanation: A Certificate of Origin confirms the country where the goods were produced.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common antiparasitic drug?
quiz.explanation: Ivermectin is a widely used antiparasitic for livestock.

quiz.q: What is the typical shipping time from India to Mombasa by sea?
quiz.explanation: Sea freight from India to Mombasa takes approximately 20-35 days.

quiz.q: Which document is NOT required for customs clearance of veterinary drugs?
quiz.explanation: Personal ID is not typically required for customs clearance of commercial goods.

quiz.q: What is the cost of a 10mÂ³ cold room?
quiz.explanation: A small cold room for pharmaceutical storage costs $5,000-$10,000.

quiz.q: Which of these is a Chinese online platform for finding suppliers?
quiz.explanation: Alibaba is a major Chinese platform for connecting with suppliers.

quiz.q: What is the typical lead time for obtaining a CPP from India?
quiz.explanation: A CPP from CDSCO in India typically takes 4-8 weeks to process.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of a reputable supplier?
quiz.explanation: A reputable supplier will provide samples for quality testing before a large order.

quiz.q: What is the main risk of buying from a trading company instead of a manufacturer?
quiz.explanation: Trading companies add a markup, so you pay a higher price than buying directly from the manufacturer.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common antibiotic used in veterinary medicine?
quiz.explanation: Oxytetracycline is a broad-spectrum antibiotic commonly used in livestock.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a proforma invoice?
options: C) To list goods and prices for a proposed sale
quiz.explanation: A proforma invoice is a preliminary bill that lists goods, quantities, and prices before a sale is finalized.

quiz.q: Which African country requires a CPP for veterinary drug registration?
options: D) Many countries, including Nigeria and Kenya
quiz.explanation: Many African countries, including Nigeria and Kenya, require a CPP for registration.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of air freight per kg from India to Africa?
quiz.explanation: Air freight for pharmaceuticals from India to Africa costs approximately $5-$8 per kg.

quiz.q: Which of these is a key component of a GMP certificate?
quiz.explanation: A GMP certificate includes details about the manufacturing site and the scope of products covered.

quiz.q: What is the recommended storage humidity for veterinary drugs?
quiz.explanation: Humidity should be kept below 60% to prevent degradation of drugs.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common vaccine for poultry?
quiz.explanation: Newcastle disease vaccine is a major poultry vaccine used across Africa.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of a data logger for temperature monitoring?
quiz.explanation: A basic data logger for temperature and humidity monitoring costs $50-$100.

quiz.q: Which of these is a benefit of attending a trade fair like IPHEX?
quiz.explanation: Trade fairs allow you to meet potential suppliers in person and build relationships.
